Geographic focus:

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical observation [YES] — Law passed in June, penalties now active
T2. Forward-looking immediate [YES] — Penalties effective immediately, ongoing impact on Shein/Temu pricing
T3. Long-term development [YES] — Penalties set to increase further from 2030

Synopsis:
France has begun enforcing fast-fashion penalties under a law passed in June, targeting ultra-high volume e-commerce retailers like Shein and Temu. Fines range from €0.25 to €12 per item (capped at 50% of pre-tax price), calculated based on volume, price, and repairability. Established European retailers (Zara, H&M) are largely unaffected due to smaller product ranges. The law compounds pressure on Shein ahead of its Hong Kong IPO, already strained by the end of EU/US duty-free thresholds. China's commerce ministry has flagged potential WTO violations.
